views.label: Request
views.note: The View asks its ViewModel; only the SDK touches the credential and the network.

views.label: Decision
views.note: The server answers 200, 401 or 403; the ViewModel maps the answer to exactly one screen state.

cards.title: One way through the layers
items: the View never calls the SDK and never reads a token: it renders a state and forwards an event, and the lint config rejects a fetch inside **/views/**
the ViewModel owns the SDK call, the status union and the retry; the hook only subscribes and schedules
the SDK never imports React, so the same client runs in the app, in a CLI and in a test runner

cards.title: The credential boundary
items: the credential is read through the TokenStore port, never from the View — a token in the bundle is a public token
auth, tenant, correlation, idempotency and client-info headers are interceptors on the SDK, not code repeated per call
no secret ever ships to the browser: tokens live in memory or in an httpOnly cookie

cards.title: One answer, one state
items: 200 with rows → ready; 200 without rows → empty; 403 → forbidden; 401 → refresh once and retry; anything else → a retryable error
the envelope is { error: { code, message, requiredPermission?, correlationId } }; the SDK normalizes it, the ViewModel maps it, the View renders it
the correlation id is shown copyable on the error screen, and a client error is reported without personal data — no token, no payload
